draft.title: Features of a time series
card: A time series is data recorded over time, plotted with time on the horizontal axis. We look at the plot for patterns.
a long-term rise or fall in the values. Seasonality is a pattern that repeats at a fixed, known period, such as every year or every week.
rises and falls that repeat, but not at a fixed period, so their timing cannot be predicted exactly. Irregular fluctuations are random ups and downs with no pattern.
Structural change is a sudden, lasting shift, such as a new road changing visitor numbers for good. An outlier is a single value far from the rest.
draft.remember: Trend is long-term, seasonality repeats on a fixed period, and a cycle repeats without one.

a.q: Ice cream sales at a kiosk in Geelong peak every summer and drop every winter, year after year. Which feature is this?
a.why: The peaks come at the same time each year, which is a fixed period, so this is seasonality. It is not a cycle, because a cycle has no fixed period.
a.clue: Look at whether the pattern repeats on a fixed schedule.

b.q: Monthly visitors to a Bendigo museum were steady for years. After a new wing opened, they jumped by about 30% and stayed there. Which feature is this?
b.why: The values shifted suddenly and stayed at the new level, which is structural change. An outlier is a single value far from the rest, so it is the tempting wrong answer, but here the shift lasted.
b.clue: Does the change last, or is it only one point?
